combat_history.event: HQ-9 batteries deployed to Woody Island in the Paracels, the first confirmed long-range SAM emplacement on a South China Sea feature.
combat_history.significance: Extended a defended-airspace bubble over contested waters.

combat_history.event: No confirmed combat interceptions; widely exercised in PLA air-defence drills.
combat_history.significance: Capability assessed from exercises and deployments, not combat.

modernization.description: Extended-range HQ-9B and the higher-tier HQ-19 build a layered air- and missile-defence shield.
modernization.impact: Broadens China's IADS toward credible ballistic-missile defence.

vulnerabilities.description: Untested against modern stealth aircraft and standoff missiles.
vulnerabilities.context: 5th-gen penetrators and decoys may degrade engagement.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Networked low-band acquisition radars and layered batteries.

vulnerabilities.description: Finite interceptors per battery are vulnerable to saturation and anti-radiation/SEAD attack.
vulnerabilities.context: A determined air campaign can attrite emitters.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Mobile batteries protecting key bases, the mainland coast and South China Sea features; naval HHQ-9 providing fleet area defence.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Networked into the national IADS with acquisition radars, fighters and shorter-range SAMs (HQ-16, HQ-7).
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Widely fielded land and naval variants; actively exported.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: S-400 offers longer-range missiles and a broader interceptor mix; HQ-9 is the indigenous Chinese answer, also operated alongside imported S-300/S-400.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: China's home-grown SAM vs the Russian system that inspired it.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Patriot PAC-3 emphasises hit-to-kill ballistic-missile defence; HQ-9 is primarily an aircraft/cruise-missile area defender with growing ABM reach.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: HQ-9 vs Patriot — competing air-defence philosophies.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: THAAD is a dedicated high-altitude ballistic-missile interceptor; its deployment to South Korea provoked strong Chinese objection.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Why China fears THAAD in Korea.

doctrine.role: Long-range area air-defence missile system and backbone of China's integrated air-defence network, with a navalised fleet-defence variant.
doctrine.employment: Mobile batteries and naval VLS engage aircraft, cruise missiles and UAVs at long range, layered with shorter-range SAMs and fighters.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Indigenise and navalise S-300-class capability into an exportable, mobile, networked family.
doctrine.threat_context: Extends China's anti-access bubble over the near seas and South China Sea features; the long-range layer of PLAN destroyer defences.
doctrine.comparison_frame: China's S-300/Patriot-class system — read against the S-400, Patriot and THAAD.
